messages:
anya: Quick heads-up — ran a priming-sensitivity sweep for the new-bridge-13b across int8 vs int4. Seeing a consistent quality drop on long multi-turn prompts with aggressive prefix compression. Sharing top-level numbers below.

micah: Can you paste the slice and the metric set?

anya: Slice = help-chat/long-multi (avg prompt ~12k tokens). Metrics = human-similarity (proxy), SROUGE, hallucination-rate, latency. Summary: int8 baseline sim=0.88, int4 aggressive sim=0.78. Token cost reduction ~30% but quality loss is ~10 pts absolute. Tail latency roughly same.

luke: Yikes — 10% absolute is material. Any idea if kv-cache hit rate changed? Compression could break cacheability.

anya: Good call. KV-cache hit dropped from 0.92 -> 0.60 with the compressed prefixes. Hallucination-rate doubled on that slice. Example of the config we ran:

```json
{
  "model": "bridge-13b",
  "quant": "int4-aggressive",
  "prefix_compression": true,
  "prefix_hashing": "token-shift",
  "kv_cache": "enabled"
}
```

reza: Two operational notes: (1) route long inputs to int8, short ones to int4; (2) try hybrid quant (first N tokens int8 then rest int4) — we've proto'd this and it helps preserve prefix fidelity.

micah: From unit-econ side: token cost per generated token int8=$0.004, int4=$0.0028. For this slice, effective savings after accounting retries/re-runs and downstream QA is only ~8% not 30%. I'll produce a small scorecard.

anya: Uploaded a quick scorecard to the shared folder: /shared/econ/priming-sensitivity/3654321987.csv (link). Product — do we want to enforce a quality floor for GTN routes? If so we need a fallback plan.

sarah-product: @anya thanks — product prefers floor sim >= 0.86 for help-chat. If int4 can't get there, fallback to int8 with canary rollout. Also need a short blurb for GTN docs about prompt length sensitivity.

micah: Ops checklist proposal: 1) add routing flag `route.long_prompts_to=int8` 2) implement canary at 10% traffic 3) monitor sim metric and latency, auto rollback if sim drops >5% vs baseline.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout for `route.long_prompts_to` started at 10% — triggered 3654324000

anya: Next steps from ML side: (1) run hybrid int8-prefix experiment (~2k reqs) (2) add prompt normalization to keep kv keys stable (3) retest with byte-level tokenization to see if compression artifacts improve. Will update scorecard and post results here.

reza: :thumbsup: I'll add the routing example to the playbook and include a short runbook entry about quantization sensitivity to tokenization. Also note: for GTN, recommend conservative default = int8 for >8k token prompts.

luke: Thanks team. If hybrid looks good, we can ship a routing quickfix that buys ~20% cost without breaking product SLAs. Keep updates short in this thread.
